question.text: The number of photons falling per second on a completely darkened plate to produce a force of <math><mn>6.62</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>-5</mn></mrow></msup><mi> </mi><mo>N</mo></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>22</mn></msup></math>. If the wavelength of the light falling is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>,</mo></math> then what is the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math>? <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6.62</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>34</mn></mrow></msup><mn> J</mn><mo> </mo><mn>s</mn></mrow></mfenced></math>

solution.text:
The energy carried by n photons per second

P=n.hcλ

As photons get absorbed by dark plate, the force experienced by the plate

F=1c. nhcλ

Or F×c=n.hcλ   as power P=force×speed


Or n=Fλh=6.62×10-5×5×10-76.62×10-34=5×1022
